## Import datasets

```{r}
mont <- read_csv('/Users/omidrezasadrmanesh/Desktop/TMU/PROJECTS/VOLUME/Montreal/Datasets/final outputs/temp_res_yr_final_mont.csv')
tor <- read_csv('/Users/omidrezasadrmanesh/Desktop/TMU/PROJECTS/VOLUME/Toronto/Datasets/final outputs/combined_results_yearly_final.csv')
cal <- read_csv('/Users/omidrezasadrmanesh/Desktop/TMU/PROJECTS/VOLUME/Calgary/Datasets/final outputs/combined_results_yearly_final.csv')

mont <- mont %>% mutate(city = "Montreal")
tor  <- tor  %>% mutate(city = "Toronto")
cal  <- cal  %>% mutate(city = "Calgary")

all_cities_cov <- bind_rows(mont, tor, cal)

# Assumes each source file is already in the LONG format seen in your data
# viewer: one row per city / coverage_type / Window / Year, with columns
# Window, coverage_type, Year, K, Observed_pct, CI_lower_pct_obs,
# CI_upper_pct_obs, Exp_pct, CI_lower_pct_exp, CI_upper_pct_exp, city.

all_cities_plot <- all_cities_cov %>%
  mutate(city = case_when(
    city == "Toronto"  ~ "Toronto (2017-2024)",
    city == "Calgary"  ~ "Calgary (2019-2024)",
    city == "Montreal" ~ "Montreal (2017-2021)",
    TRUE ~ city
  )) %>%
  mutate(city = factor(city, levels = c(
    "Montreal (2017-2021)",
    "Toronto (2017-2024)",
    "Calgary (2019-2024)"
  )))
```

## Shared helpers

```{r}
window_levels <- c("±1 month (w=3)", "±2 months (w=5)", "±3 months (w=7)")
window_labels  <- c("3 Months", "5 Months", "7 Months")

prep_coverage_data <- function(data) {
  df <- data %>%
    mutate(window = factor(Window, levels = window_levels, labels = window_labels))
  lines <- df %>%
    dplyr::select(Year, city, window, Observed_pct, Exp_pct) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(Observed_pct, Exp_pct),
                 names_to = "type", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(type = recode(type,
                         "Observed_pct" = "Observed",
                         "Exp_pct"      = "Expected"))
  ci <- df %>%
    dplyr::select(Year, city, window,
                  CI_lower_pct_obs, CI_upper_pct_obs,
                  CI_lower_pct_exp, CI_upper_pct_exp) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols      = -c(Year, city, window),
      names_to  = c(".value", "type"),
      names_pattern = "(CI_lower_pct|CI_upper_pct)_(obs|exp)"
    ) %>%
    rename(lo = CI_lower_pct, hi = CI_upper_pct) %>%
    mutate(type = recode(type, "obs" = "Observed", "exp" = "Expected")) %>%
    filter(!is.na(lo), !is.na(hi))
  list(lines = lines, ci = ci)
}

plot_coverage_9panel <- function(lines, ci) {

  ci_obs <- ci %>% filter(type == "Observed")
  ci_exp <- ci %>% filter(type == "Expected")

  ggplot(lines, aes(Year, value, colour = type, linetype = type)) +

    # Expected CI first so observed renders on top
    geom_ribbon(data = ci_exp,
                aes(x = Year, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
                fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.35,
                colour = "grey40", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6,
                inherit.aes = FALSE) +

    # Observed CI
    geom_ribbon(data = ci_obs,
                aes(x = Year, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
                fill = "#E15759", alpha = 0.18,
                colour = NA, inherit.aes = FALSE) +

    geom_line(linewidth = 1.0) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = type), size = 1.8) +

    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c("Observed" = "#E15759", "Expected" = "#4E79A7"),
      name = "Coverage"
    ) +
    scale_linetype_manual(
      values = c("Observed" = "solid", "Expected" = "dashed"),
      name = "Coverage"
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c("Observed" = 16, "Expected" = 21),
      name = "Coverage"
    ) +

    facet_grid(window ~ city, scales = "free_x") +

    labs(
      x = "Year", y = "KSI Coverage (%)",
      caption = "Shaded bands = 95% CI  |  Red fill = Observed  ·  Grey dashed outline = Expected"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      legend.position    = "right",
      legend.key.width   = unit(1.2, "cm"),
      strip.text.x       = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold",
                                        margin = margin(b = 4, t = 4)),
      strip.text.y       = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold",
                                        margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4)),
      panel.border       = element_rect(colour = "grey70", fill = NA),
      strip.background   = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = "grey70"),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      plot.caption       = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40", hjust = 0)
    )
}
```

## Either temporary or permanent counters plot

```{r}
# Montreal has no "either" rows, so use its "temporary" rows as the stand-in
# for that city in this plot (temporary is its only counter type).
any_source <- bind_rows(
  all_cities_plot %>% filter(!str_detect(city, "Montreal"), coverage_type == "either"),
  all_cities_plot %>% filter(str_detect(city, "Montreal"),  coverage_type == "temporary")
)

any_data <- prep_coverage_data(any_source)
plot_coverage_9panel(any_data$lines, any_data$ci)

ggsave("coverage_any_3cities.png", width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
```

For Linda's Poster: Toronto Only

```{r}
# 1. Filter data for Toronto AND select coverage type
plot_tor <- all_cities_plot %>% 
  filter(
    str_detect(city, "Toronto"), 
    coverage_type == "either" # Adjust coverage_type if needed
  )

# 2. Prep data using your function
tor_data <- prep_coverage_data(plot_tor)

# 3. Create a dedicated single-city plot function with Windows as Columns
plot_coverage_toronto <- function(lines, ci) {
  
  ci_obs <- ci %>% filter(type == "Observed")
  ci_exp <- ci %>% filter(type == "Expected")

  ggplot(lines, aes(Year, value, colour = type, linetype = type)) +

    # Expected CI
    geom_ribbon(data = ci_exp,
                aes(x = Year, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
                fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.35,
                colour = "grey40", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6,
                inherit.aes = FALSE) +

    # Observed CI
    geom_ribbon(data = ci_obs,
                aes(x = Year, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
                fill = "#E15759", alpha = 0.18,
                colour = NA, inherit.aes = FALSE) +

    geom_line(linewidth = 1.0) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = type), size = 1.8) +

    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c("Observed" = "#E15759", "Expected" = "#4E79A7"),
      name = "Coverage"
    ) +
    scale_linetype_manual(
      values = c("Observed" = "solid", "Expected" = "dashed"),
      name = "Coverage"
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c("Observed" = 16, "Expected" = 21),
      name = "Coverage"
    ) +

    # MONTHS/WINDOWS ARE NOW TOP COLUMNS:
    facet_grid(. ~ window, scales = "free_x") +

    labs(
      x = "Year", y = "KSI Coverage (%)",
      caption = "Shaded bands = 95% CI  |  Red fill = Observed  ·  Grey dashed outline = Expected"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      legend.position    = "right",
      legend.key.width   = unit(1.2, "cm"),
      strip.text.x       = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 4, t = 4)),
      panel.border       = element_rect(colour = "grey70", fill = NA),
      strip.background   = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = "grey70"),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      plot.caption       = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40", hjust = 0)
    )
}

# 4. Generate & Save Plot
p_tor <- plot_coverage_toronto(tor_data$lines, tor_data$ci)
print(p_tor)

# Adjust height since it is only 1 row now
ggsave("coverage_toronto_only.png", plot = p_tor, width = 11, height = 4.5, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
```

Windows on the side

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Filter for Toronto and select the relevant coverage type
plot_tor <- all_cities_plot %>% 
  filter(
    str_detect(city, "Toronto"), 
    coverage_type == "either"  # Adjust if a different coverage_type was used in Fig 4
  )

# 2. Prepare data
tor_data <- prep_coverage_data(plot_tor)

# 3. Build Figure 4 specifically for Toronto with windows along the side
plot_fig4_toronto <- function(lines, ci) {
  
  ci_obs <- ci %>% filter(type == "Observed")
  ci_exp <- ci %>% filter(type == "Expected")

  ggplot(lines, aes(Year, value, colour = type, linetype = type)) +

    # Expected CI (grey)
    geom_ribbon(data = ci_exp,
                aes(x = Year, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
                fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.35,
                colour = "grey40", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6,
                inherit.aes = FALSE) +

    # Observed CI (red)
    geom_ribbon(data = ci_obs,
                aes(x = Year, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
                fill = "#E15759", alpha = 0.18,
                colour = NA, inherit.aes = FALSE) +

    geom_line(linewidth = 1.0) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = type), size = 1.8) +

    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c("Observed" = "#E15759", "Expected" = "#4E79A7"),
      name = "Coverage"
    ) +
    scale_linetype_manual(
      values = c("Observed" = "solid", "Expected" = "dashed"),
      name = "Coverage"
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c("Observed" = 16, "Expected" = 21),
      name = "Coverage"
    ) +

    # WINDOWS ALONG THE SIDE (Rows = window, Columns = none)
    facet_grid(window ~ ., scales = "free_x") +

    labs(
      x = "Year", 
      y = "KSI Coverage (%)",
      caption = "Shaded bands = 95% CI  |  Red fill = Observed  ·  Grey dashed outline = Expected"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      legend.position    = "right",
      legend.key.width   = unit(1.2, "cm"),
      strip.text.y       = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4)),
      panel.border       = element_rect(colour = "grey70", fill = NA),
      strip.background   = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = "grey70"),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      plot.caption       = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40", hjust = 0)
    )
}

# 4. Generate plot and save with a tall aspect ratio
fig4_toronto <- plot_fig4_toronto(tor_data$lines, tor_data$ci)
fig4_toronto

ggsave("Figure4_Toronto_Only.png", plot = fig4_toronto, width = 7, height = 9, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
```
